models_evaluated: autonomous AI for diabetic eye disease testing

links.outcome: Change in DED testing adherence by race across AI-switched vs non-AI sites
links.effect: Adherence for Black/African Americans rose 12.2 percentage points at AI-switched sites vs a 0.6% point decrease at non-AI sites (p<0.001); Asian–Black adherence gap shrank from 15.6% to 3.5%.
links.quote: Second, the adherence rate for Black/African Americans increased by 12.2 percentage points within AI-switched sites but decreased by 0.6% points within non-AI sites (p < 0.001), suggesting that autonomous AI deployment improved access to retinal evaluation for historically disadvantaged populations.

unlisted_practices: Deploying autonomous AI diabetic eye exam at primary care point of care to increase screening adherence

screen.reason: The study evaluates the real-world deployment impact of an autonomous AI tool for diabetic eye disease on adherence and health equity compared to non-AI sites, rather than testing a specific implementation guardrail or deployment practice.
